prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: ফসল মৌসুমভিত্তিক বপন, কর্তন ও ফলন সূচি (language bn).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "ফসল" · longest unbreakable word 69px · one-line width 149px
  col 2: header "বপন" · longest unbreakable word 66px · one-line width 263px
  col 3: header "কাটা" · longest unbreakable word 68px · one-line width 239px
  col 4: header "ফলন (টন/হেক্টর)" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 108px
  col 5: header "মন্তব্য" · longest unbreakable word 68px · one-line width 1035px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare crops by their sowing and harvest windows, yield index, and accompanying notes in a seasonal schedule.","reading":"Row by row: identify the crop in column 1, compare the paired sowing and harvest timing in columns 2–3, read the yield in column 4, then consult the comment in column 5.","groups":["Columns 2 and 3 form a paired sowing–harvest timeline and should have similar widths so the two dates can be compared across rows.","Column 4 is a compact numeric attribute attached to the timing pair and needs much less width than the date columns.","Column 1 is the row identifier and should stay strong; column 5 is secondary commentary whose width depends on whether notes or schedule comparison is prioritized."],"keep_intact":["Crop names and variety identifiers such as বোরো ধান (উফশী), আমন ধান (স্থানীয়), গম (বারি গম-৩৩), সরিষা (বারি সরিষা-১৪)","Numeric yield values and the unit টন/হেক্টর","Month names and date words, which may wrap at spaces but must not break mid-word"],"may_wrap":["Sowing and harvest date ranges in columns 2–3 at natural word spaces","Long comments in column 5","Longer crop names only at spaces or parentheses if the crop column is tightened"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [170, 150, 145, 85, 169] · table 720×1138px · row heights [83, 199, 153, 176, 176, 176, 176] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [140, 175, 170, 80, 154] · table 720×1301px · row heights [83, 222, 176, 199, 199, 199, 222] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 9 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [170, 120, 115, 75, 239] · table 720×836px · row heights [83, 153, 106, 129, 129, 106, 129] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
